Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md:

  • SSR first. Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.

  • GraphQL for composed pages. Where a page assembles many entries, the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.

  • Live preview. When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on postMessage events from Studio.

  • Asset delivery. Images come from images.ctfassets.net. The storefront generates srcset, sizes, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint. images.ctfassets.net is preconnected from the document head.

  • SSR cache TTL. 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache — the TTL is the fallback if a webhook drops.

  • CDN rate limit. 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic — risk only during burst republish events.

This section documents the resolved design for how SFCC product and category IDs are embedded in Contentful content models, how MRT resolves them at render time, and how conditional component rendering is implemented based on those IDs. This is the core design question the spike(SFCC-123) was tasked to answer.

Content Model: How to Store SFCC IDs

SFCC product and category IDs are stored as plain Short Text fields on the Contentful content type. They are not localized — they are structural fields that identify what SFCC data the editorial entry is associated with, and the value does not change per locale.

Render-Time Resolution in MRT (SSR)

At SSR time, MRT fetches all published entries of a given content type for the current locale via CDA. Before passing entries to React components, the SSR layer filters them by matching the SFCC ID field against the current page context. The component never sees unmatched entries — it receives only the entries that should render.

Homepage

No SFCC ID context

This is a critical implication of the ID-based filtering pattern. If SSR cache keys do not include the SFCC category or product ID, the cached response for one category will be incorrectly served to a different category. 

Cache key rule: any page whose SSR output depends on sfccCategoryId filtering MUST include the category ID in its MRT cache key. Same rule applies to sfccProductId on PDPs. Failure to do this will cause editorial components to appear on the wrong category/product pages.

Component Contract

React components that render SFCC-ID-targeted content must be written to the following contract:

  • The component does NOT receive raw Contentful entries — it receives pre-filtered entries from the SSR layer.

  • The component does NOT contain any SFCC ID comparison logic.

  • The component renders all entries it receives, in the order it receives them.

  • If the entries array is empty (no match), the component renders nothing — null return, no DOM output.

Environment & Locale Configuration

The platform uses a single Contentful Space with one Environment per delivery tier (dev → test → sit → staging → uat → production), promoted sequentially. Production uses an alias (CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production) for zero-downtime releases. Nine locales are configured across eight storefronts, with en as the default fallback. Full environment setup, alias management, and locale configuration are maintained in Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations.

Locale Rules for Content Modellers

  • Translatable fields (headline, body copy, CTA text, alt text) → set localized: true in the content type definition.

  • Structural fields (asset links, layout flags, product IDs) → set localized: false — shared across all locales. Canonical examples of non-localized structural fields: sfccCategoryId and sfccProductId. These are SFCC identifiers and do not vary by locale.

  • Fallback chain: if a locale (e.g. fr) has no content for a field, Contentful falls back to en automatically. Authors only fill fields they want to override.

  • Translation pipeline: Transperfect is the translation partner (HPC-006). Strategy is under discussion — Contentful squad to own.

Key Design Decisions

Decision

Choice

Rationale

Single Contentful Space for all 8 storefronts

One Space, per-locale content fields

Locale model handles per-storefront variation. Avoids content duplication and reduces operational overhead vs one space per storefront.

Schema as code — not hand-created in UI

Git-managed definitions deployed via npm run sync:contentful

Prevents schema drift, enables code review of content model changes, and gives CI visibility of structural changes before production.

CDA token in browser bundle (delivery only)

Delivery API token is browser-safe

CDA tokens are read-only and scoped to one environment. Preview (CPA) and Management (CMA) tokens are never deployed to MRT or exposed to the browser.

Production alias instead of fixed environment name

CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production resolves to an alias

Enables zero-downtime releases: flip the alias to a pre-tested release clone without redeploying MRT. Requires Contentful Enterprise plan.

ISR cache invalidation via webhook on publish

Contentful fires HMAC-signed webhook → MRT invalidates cache

Pages are server-rendered and cached. Without cache invalidation, published content changes would not appear until cache TTL expires. Webhook makes updates near-real-time.

Graceful degradation for CMS unavailability

Render page without editorial content if Contentful is down

Commerce functionality must never be blocked by CMS availability. Editorial content is an enhancement, not a dependency.

Contentful SDK v11 — no connection pool isolation hook

Mitigate via graceful degradation, not pool isolation

SDK v11 does not expose a dispatcher hook for custom connection pooling. Primary mitigation is graceful degradation.

SFCC ID references in Contentful content model

Plain ShortText fields (sfccProductId, sfccCategoryId), localized: false. Filtering in MRT SSR, not in the React component.

ID fields are structural, not editorial — they do not vary by locale. Resolution and conditional rendering happen entirely in the MRT SSR layer. The Contentful entry is the editorial shell; SFCC provides the commerce data it wraps. Components remain dumb and reusable. Cache keys must include the SFCC ID to avoid cross-context cache collisions.

## SFCC-123 TSD — validation audit (pass 3)

**Sources re-checked this pass:** TSD page 346783750 (v15, content grepped for each anchor), all comments, ops page 318472193 (v7), Jira (SFCC-67, SFCC-14), codebase (`zimmermann-pwa`).

**Drift since last audit:** none. Version unchanged (15), comment set unchanged, no new Tim/Jhoan replies, `.docs/spikes` untouched.

### Flag validation — all 10 reproduce, none overturned, none new

**High severity (would mislead the incoming squad):**
1. **CMA-secret contradiction — STANDS.** TSD Bootstrap says "GitHub Actions secret ✅ Complete"; its own Blockers #5 + Open-Items #4 say Incomplete; **ops page v7 item 9 = incomplete** (re-read this pass). Three-way conflict.

3. **Locale count contradictory — STANDS.** Content contains **both** "Nine locales" (body) and "11-locale" (Blockers #1). Truth = 9.
4. **Sprint-2 sprint/epic errors — STANDS.** SFCC-67 & SFCC-14 both still in the Sprint-2 table; Jira re-confirmed SFCC-67 = Story under **Checkout Flow & Delivery** (Sprint 4) and **SFCC-14 = Epic** (Returns, Sprint 7).

**Medium:**
5. **Handoff "[FOR UPDATE]" — STANDS.** Marker still in content; Tim's "I will update" open.
6. **SFCC-ID pattern design-only + PLP spike gap + naming — STANDS.** No `sfccCategoryId/sfccProductId/plpInlineGridInsert` in code; Tim's required PLP pagination spike still unreferenced; `sfccProductId` ≠ existing `productId`.
7. **New Relic sourced from a "Not Required" draft doc — STANDS.** "Not Required" still in content; cited doc (307134467) is a DRAFT reconciliation doc, not the authoritative Observability deck.
8. **Product-image ownership asserted vs undecided — STANDS.** Still asserts SFCC BM; DC002 decision page still empty.

**Low:**
9. **Self-referential "Tell No Lies" link — STANDS.** `x/BoCrF` (→ this page) still in content.
10. **Footer/homepage "risk is accepted" — STANDS.** Still present; in tension with "never block" and Tim's cache re-think.

No drift — still v15, **24 comments unchanged, no new replies.** Findings validated a fourth time. Below is the deliverable: a **send-ready feedback set for Jhoan**, written in Tim's review posture — challenge each claim, kill drift, correct the facts, assign owners, and capture spikes/to-dos. I've triaged it the way Tim does (fix-before-share vs validate vs capture-as-to-do vs raise-with-leads).

---

**Hi Jhoan — really solid progress on this, the SFCC-ID reference pattern in particular is exactly what the spike needed. Before we share it with the incoming squad, a few things to tighten. Grouped by priority.**

### 🔴 Fix before we share
1. **Bootstrap Status → "CMA token as GitHub Actions secret."** You've got this as ✅ Complete, but your own Blockers #5 and Open Items #4 say it's incomplete, and the Setup & Ops page (checklist item 9) also has it incomplete. Let's land on one status — if it's genuinely done, tick it everywhere and I'll confirm with the Integration Lead; otherwise mark it incomplete consistently.
2. **Integration Architecture → "Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md."** This lists SSR-first fetch, GraphQL, and the publish webhook as current behaviour, and `useContentful.ts` sits under "Already built" — but the live hook is browser-side REST; there's no GraphQL client, SSR editorial fetch, or webhook receiver in the repo yet. Let's split "built today" from "target architecture (to build)" so the squad doesn't assume SSR editorial is live. Also — where's the webhook receiver going to live, and is that this-integration scope or a separate story?
3. **Blockers #1 — locale count.** The body correctly says nine locales (matches `config/sites.js` and the ops page), but Blocker #1 still says "confirm the canonical 11-locale set." That's resolved — it's **9** (the "11" in `02-contentful.md` is wrong; `en-AU` is BM's default that the AU site narrows to `en`). Let's close Blocker #1 as resolved and drop the 11-locale wording.
4. **Sprint-2 content-types table.** Checkout Trust Messaging (SFCC-67) lives under *Checkout Flow & Delivery* = **Sprint 4**, and Returns/Refund (SFCC-14) is an **Epic** (you flagged this in the capability table already) = **Sprint 7** — so neither belongs in Sprint 2. Let's move them to their real sprints, and for SFCC-14 reference the child story once it's raised.
5. **Handoff Boundary — still "[FOR UPDATE]."** This is the first thing the incoming squad reads, and the ownership split (especially the Z.immerse rows) reads muddled. Tim owns the update — let's sync with him and get it finalised before we share.

### 🟡 Validate before finalising (have we checked these to the designs?)
6. **Sprint-2 content types.** You rightly noted these are assumed, not confirmed — SFCC-82/190/67 defer their content model to stories not yet created, and none map to an HPC req in 04.1.1. Let's get the **Emma & Dani authoring session** booked before we lock those field sets.
7. **Mega Menu fields.** Design-dependent — SFCC-96 needs the Figma spec first. Let's mark those fields provisional pending the design.

### 🟠 Capture as to-dos / spikes (not blocking now)
8. **PLP Inline Grid Insert.** The SFCC-ID pattern presents the PLP inject as resolved, but Tim flagged we still need a spike to confirm we can inject a Contentful item into the SFCC PLP grid **without breaking item counts / pagination.** Let's add a "pending feasibility spike" note and raise the card (Hazel's already tagged).
9. **PDP Accordion — mixed content.** Contentful tabs + SFCC-sourced tabs (Details & Care, Size & Fit) in one accordion, with exact SFCC fields TBD. Good that you flagged it — let's make sure the mixed-content-rendering spike card gets raised too.
10. **MRT-apps section.** As agreed, we'll scratch this once Gideon and I finish the separate MRT-apps TSD and just link it here.

### 🔵 Raise with leads / POs (decisions outside our control)
11. **Error Handling & Monitoring — New Relic.** The section's well-structured, two things: (a) it's anchored to the *Integration Reconciliation* working doc (`x/A4BOEg`), which is a **draft** and actually lists New Relic as **"Not Required"** — let's re-anchor to the **Accenture Observability, Tracing & Security Assurance deck**, which is the authoritative source; (b) New Relic isn't procured or on the credentials tracker yet — I'm raising procurement with Emma/IT, so let's keep the alert policies framed as "recommended, pending procurement."
12. **"What is NOT in Contentful" → product imagery.** You've asserted it's SFCC BM — that's the likely answer, but it isn't decided: the PWA TSD says imagery is served from Contentful, and the **DC002 decision page is empty**. Let's mark it "pending DC002" rather than stating it, and I'll push for the decision (Digital/Integration).
13. **Cache / graceful degradation.** Since footer and homepage always render from Contentful, a full CDA outage gives a broken bare page, which you've noted as "risk accepted." Let's take a firmer position with Tim — is Contentful effectively a hard dependency there, and do we need a minimal static fallback?

### ⚪ Minor / housekeeping
14. **"Tell No Lies" link** (Didomi row + monitoring) points back to this page (`x/BoCrF`) — repoint or drop it.
15. **Field naming** — you've used `sfccProductId`, but the one product-ID field already in code is `productId` (`SFCC_PRODUCT_ID_FIELD`). Let's align so we don't introduce a second convention.

**Net:** items 1-5 are the gate to sharing this; 6-7 need a design/authoring check; 8-10 are spikes/to-dos to raise; 11-13 need a lead/PO decision (I'll drive 11 and 12). Nice work overall — this is close.

**Fix before we share**

1. **Bootstrap Status, CMA token as GitHub Actions secret.** This is marked Complete, but it should be Incomplete: the Setup & Ops runbook (page 318472193, checklist item 9) is the source of truth for setup state and has it incomplete, and the content-type sync/migrate steps aren't wired into CI yet, so the token isn't in use. Your own Blockers #5 and Open Items #4 also say incomplete. Let's set it to Incomplete to match the runbook. (If it's since been added, let's update the runbook first, then the TSD.)
2. **Integration Architecture, "Key behaviours confirmed in 02-contentful.md."** SSR-first fetch, GraphQL, and the publish webhook are listed as current behaviour, and useContentful.ts sits under "Already built", but the live hook is browser-side REST, the experience route also fetches client-side, and there's no GraphQL client, SSR editorial fetch, or webhook receiver in the repo yet. Let's split "built today" from "target architecture (to build)" so the squad doesn't assume SSR editorial is live. Also: where will the webhook receiver live, and is that this-integration scope or a separate story?

7. **PLP Inline Grid Insert.** The ID pattern presents the PLP inject as resolved, but Tim flagged we still need a spike to confirm we can inject a Contentful item into the SFCC PLP grid without breaking item counts or pagination. Let's add a "pending feasibility spike" note and raise the card (Hazel is tagged).

**Raise with leads / POs (decisions outside our control)**

10. **Error Handling & Monitoring, New Relic.** Two things: (a) it's currently anchored to the Integration Reconciliation working doc, which is a draft and actually lists New Relic as "Not Required", so please re-anchor to the "CDN, eCDN & Security Configuration" page (339935324), which references the Accenture Observability, Tracing & Security Assurance deck and holds the Log Centre to New Relic streaming checklist; (b) New Relic isn't procured or on the credentials tracker yet - I've already raised procurement with Emma/IT and we're pending their reply, so let's frame the alert policies as "recommended, pending procurement."

Really close, nice work. Happy to pair on any of these.
